summary: NYISO files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-517-000. They set up Large Load Integration Procedures, two new withdrawal services instead of the three PJM-style services, curtailment of non-firm service when the local price reaches $200/MWh, and a State Exempt Load Project exception for New York's resource adequacy rules. The New York transmission owners filed cost recovery terms separately.
ask: Accept without modification, effective from February 1, 2027 to May 1, 2029 by part; keep the show cause case in abeyance, end it for NYISO on acceptance, and allow 28 days for comments.

points.point: NYISO says the revisions fully answer FERC's concerns within its own filing rights.
points.quote: They are intended to fully satisfy the concerns raised by the Commission

points.point: It proposes Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service rather than the three services FERC created for PJM.
NYISO explains why it will not adopt the three PJM co-location services.
points.quote: Part V explains why the NYISO is not proposing to adopt the three new transmission services that the Commission established in the PJM Co-Location Order

points.point: Non-firm service would be curtailed when the local price reaches $200 per megawatt-hour.
points.quote: establish a rule under which Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would be curtailed when the applicable nodal Locational- Based Marginal Price (“LBMP”) for a Large Load reaches $200 MW/h

points.point: A State Exempt Load Project exception is meant to respect the New York PSC's resource adequacy authority.
points.quote: the State Exempt Load Project exception, that is intended to reconcile the NYISO’s reliability responsibilities with the NYPSC’s resource adequacy authority

points.point: The New York transmission owners file a separate two-party cost recovery agreement.
points.quote: the NYTOs will submit a new two-party pro forma cost recovery agreement to address the cost- shifting issues discussed in the Show Cause Order

points.point: NYISO asks FERC to keep the show cause case in abeyance and end it for NYISO if the filing is accepted.
points.quote: If the Commission accepts this filing it should also issue an order terminating the Show Cause Order proceeding with respect to the NYISO.

points.point: Effective dates run from February 2027 to May 2029.
points.quote: the NYISO is requesting a February 1, 2027 effective date for the LLIP-related tariff provisions

points.point: NYISO asks for 28 days for comments instead of 21.
points.quote: the NYISO asks that the Commission briefly extend the comment period on this filing from the standard twenty-one days to twenty-eight days

points.point: The filing won the required supermajority of NYISO stakeholders.
points.quote: received the super- majority stakeholder approval required under the NYISO’s shared governance model

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-12 show cause order for NYISO. The New York transmission owners and the non-incumbent owners filed their own parts separately the same day.

figures.label: Price at which non-firm service is curtailed
